messages.author: ef8e4d99c49af174
messages.subject: k-truncated negative binomial model
parts: Is it possible to estimate a model for a dependent variable that is k-truncated with k>0, in glmmTMB? I am working with a data set with a count variable for which the exact value is not known if it is 4 or below. The reason for this is protection of privacy, the data set is aggregated from data on individuals that are considered at risk of identification if there are few individuals within one specific institution one particular year. Apart from this the data set is suitable for analysis with glmmTMB, there are a number of institutions and observations for multiple years within each institution. Since this is a question of whether it is possible to estimate a specific type of model I do not included a data set here, but if preferable I may prepare an example where the problem is "solved" by a not particularly satisfactory ad hoc procedure by setting all such values equal to 2.

messages.author: fd4f3538f907404b
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] k-truncated negative binomial model
parts:
To be precise this is a k-censored distribution rather than
k-truncated; events with k<4 aren't excluded from the data set,
they're just reported as k=4.

A crude way to do this would be something like

if (x[i]==4) {
cumprob=0;
for (s=0; s<=4; s++) {
cumprob += dnbinom2(s, mu, var, 0);
}
nll -= log(cumprob);
} else {
nll -= dnbinom2(x[i], mu, var, 1);
}

It would be more efficient if there were a pnbinom2 function for the
(log) cumulative probability.

Corrections welcome (I'm not fluent in TMB ...)
